raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence", "note": "The shutdown may also signal a quiet fear that they won't be able to figure out what they're supposed to figure out — so it's safer to not engage at all." },
  "read": "Almost-18 means they're standing at the edge of a life they haven't chosen yet, and every college conversation feels like a mirror asking 'who are you?' when they genuinely don't know. Shutting down is self-protection: if they don't engage, they can't give the wrong answer and feel like a failure in front of the person whose opinion matters most.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Back off entirely to keep the peace — which signals that the future is too scary to even talk about, and leaves them more alone in the anxiety, not less." },
  "mentorMove": "Keep the door open and the pressure off the outcome: make it normal to think out loud without needing a finished answer, so the conversation stops feeling like a verdict and starts feeling like exploration they're doing with you, not under you.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Thinking about what comes next is not optional — we talk about it, even when it's uncomfortable.",
    "You don't have to have it figured out, but you do have to stay in the conversation with me."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "When you talk about it, what form that takes — a drive, a walk, a text thread, whatever gets you actually talking.",
    "What the answer looks like — college, gap year, trade, something we haven't named yet — all of it is on the table.",
    "How fast you move toward a decision — we can go slow as long as we keep moving."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I want to talk about something, and I want to say upfront — I'm not coming at you with a plan or a deadline. I've noticed this topic tends to shut things down between us, and I don't want that. I'd rather have you than be right about what your life should look like." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When the future stuff comes up and you go quiet — what's actually happening for you in that moment? Is it that you don't know yet, or is it that you feel like you're supposed to know and you don't, or something else entirely? I'm genuinely asking, not setting up a lecture." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "What if we just agreed that not knowing is the starting point, not the problem? Like, what would make it feel less like a test every time it comes up? Because I want to be someone you think this through with, not someone you're hiding from." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "Here's where I stand: I'm not dropping this, because I think you're someone who is capable of building a life you're actually proud of — I believe that completely. But I need you to stay in the conversation with me, even when it's uncomfortable. Not because I have the answer, but because you shouldn't be carrying this alone. Can we agree to keep talking, even when we don't get anywhere fast?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "The goal isn't a college decision — it's that your kid learns they can sit with an open, uncomfortable question without collapsing or running. Every time you hold this conversation without flinching and without forcing, you're teaching them that uncertainty about identity is survivable, which is maybe the most useful thing they'll take into adulthood."
}
situation: My almost-18-year-old shuts down every time college or life after graduation comes up.
